title: S0310 (2020 Regular): Three-dimensional Printed Firearms

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, Florida); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Florida text (Introduced, 2019-09-17; official copy, https://www.flsenate.gov/Session/Bill/2020/310/BillText/Filed/HTML (LegiScan doc 2053704))
provenance.note: Introduced version (filed 2019-09-17); no passage vote on file. Para. (2)(a) lists the banned plastics (PET, polycarbonate, PLA, ABS); (4) requires relinquishing or destroying such firearms, expiring December 31, 2020.

operative_text:
Section 1 (new s. 790.224(1), F.S.): As used in this section, the term “3D-printed firearm” means a firearm that is created using a three-dimensional printer or an additive manufacturing process, or a similar device or process, and that is capable of firing one or more projectiles.
Section 1 (new s. 790.224(2), F.S.): On or after January 1, 2021, a person may not print, transfer, import into this state, distribute, sell, possess, or give to another person a 3D-printed firearm that:
Section 1 (new s. 790.224(2)(b), F.S.): Does not contain at least 4 ounces of a metal detectable by metal detectors used for security checks.
Section 1 (new s. 790.224(3), F.S.): A person who violates subsection (2) commits a felony of the third degree, punishable as provided in s. 775.082, s. 775.083, or s. 775.084.
